title: Bruce W. Brackett
lessons: Hurt people hurt people, and healing people heal themselves as well as they heal others.
The harm you carry spills onto others. So does the healing.
Sit down and untie your knots.
You can't show up for anyone until you deal with what's tangled inside you.
When you're done with the bullsh*t, you drop the chains.
You decide what you carry. Nobody can set it down for you.
When you're willing, the readiness will come.
You don't have to feel ready to start. Willing is enough.
Without my sobriety, I would have nothing.
Everything he has now is built on that one decision.
You don't have to keep every old hurt on display. Clear the shelves.

guestCard.bio: Bruce W. Brackett is an author, visual artist, and speaker. His book How to Breathe While Suffocating draws on his personal history and recovery, themes he also discusses through his public speaking and social media.

help.name: SAMHSA's National Helpline
help.notes: Free, confidential, 24/7, 365 days a year. Treatment referral and information for people facing substance use or mental health issues. English and Spanish.

meta.blurb: Bruce W. Brackett describes sobriety as the foundation beneath the life he has now. Getting there meant facing experiences he had spent years trying to survive.
